question.:question/worked-solution:
The general equation of a circle with radius $r$ centered at the point $(a,b)$ is 

$$
(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}={r}^{2}.
$$

Let's compare the general equation to our equation side-by-side as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2} & ={r}^{2} \\ (x-2)^{2}+(y-3)^{2} & =6 \\ (x-2)^{2}+(y-3)^{2} & =(\sqrt{6})^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We see that $a=2,$ $b=3,$ and $r=\sqrt{6}.$ 

Therefore, the circle is centered at $(2,3)$ and its radius is $\sqrt{6}.$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2} & ={r}^{2} \\ (x-10)^{2}+(y+\frac{8}{3})^{2} & =5 \\ (x-10)^{2}+(y-(- \frac{8}{3}))^{2} & =(\sqrt{5})^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
The general equation of a circle with radius $r$ centered at the point $(a,b)$ is 

$$
(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}={r}^{2}.
$$

Let's compare the general equation to our equation side-by-side as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2} & ={r}^{2} \\ (x+8)^{2}+(y+\frac{7}{3})^{2} & =7 \\ (x-(-8))^{2}+(y-(- \frac{7}{3}))^{2} & =(\sqrt{7})^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We see that $a=-8,$ $b=- \frac{7}{3},$ and $r=\sqrt{7}.$ 

Therefore, the circle is centered at $(-8,- \frac{7}{3})$ and its radius is $\sqrt{7}.$

(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}={r}^{2}.

question.:question/worked-solution:
The general equation of a circle with radius $r$ centered at the point $(a,b)$ is 

$$
(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}={r}^{2}.
$$

Let's compare the general equation to our equation side-by-side as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2} & ={r}^{2} \\ (x-\frac{3}{2})^{2}+(y+\frac{2}{3})^{2} & =63 \\ (x-\frac{3}{2})^{2}+(y-(- \frac{2}{3}))^{2} & =(3 \sqrt{7})^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The radius is the positive square root of the right-hand side:

$$
r=\sqrt{63}=\sqrt{9\cdot 7}=3 \sqrt{7}.
$$

We see that $a=\frac{3}{2},$ $b=- \frac{2}{3},$ and $r=3 \sqrt{7}.$ 

Therefore, the circle is centered at $(\frac{3}{2},- \frac{2}{3})$ and its radius is $3 \sqrt{7}.$

question.:question/worked-solution:
The general equation of a circle with radius $r$ centered at the point $(a,b)$ is 

$$
(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}={r}^{2}.
$$

Let's compare the general equation to our equation side-by-side as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2} & ={r}^{2} \\ (x+\frac{2}{3})^{2}+(y+\frac{5}{2})^{2} & =98 \\ (x-(- \frac{2}{3}))^{2}+(y-(- \frac{5}{2}))^{2} & =(7 \sqrt{2})^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The radius is the positive square root of the right-hand side:

$$
r=\sqrt{98}=\sqrt{49\cdot 2}=7 \sqrt{2}.
$$

We see that $a=- \frac{2}{3},$ $b=- \frac{5}{2},$ and $r=7 \sqrt{2}.$ 

Therefore, the circle is centered at $(- \frac{2}{3},- \frac{5}{2})$ and its radius is $7 \sqrt{2}.$

question.:question/worked-solution:
The general equation of a circle with radius $r$ centered at the point $(a,b)$ is 

$$
(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}={r}^{2}.
$$

Let's compare the general equation to our equation side-by-side as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2} & ={r}^{2} \\ (x+\frac{1}{2})^{2}+(y+\frac{5}{3})^{2} & =75 \\ (x-(- \frac{1}{2}))^{2}+(y-(- \frac{5}{3}))^{2} & =(5 \sqrt{3})^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The radius is the positive square root of the right-hand side:

$$
r=\sqrt{75}=\sqrt{25\cdot 3}=5 \sqrt{3}.
$$

We see that $a=- \frac{1}{2},$ $b=- \frac{5}{3},$ and $r=5 \sqrt{3}.$ 

Therefore, the circle is centered at $(- \frac{1}{2},- \frac{5}{3})$ and its radius is $5 \sqrt{3}.$
